# Lawyers in the loop: what changed in v1.1.0

From v1.0.0 (2026-11-22, `50827d71a`) to v1.1.0 (2026-11-23, this release), paragraph by paragraph.

7 paragraphs added, 0 removed, 5 changed in place, 51 unchanged. About 383 words added and 6 removed. Insertions are marked like this, deletions like this; unchanged runs are folded to one line; figures appear as their file names.

[all versions](../lawyers-in-the-loop.md)

1 unchanged paragraph

Summary: My agent teams have plenty of checks and controls, and too many of them end with a question that only I can answer, in a session I have to visit. So we are designing a way to delegate my authority without giving it away. My key stays on my own device. I sign, on pki.sgit.ai, a delegation to one decisions agent: this key, held in this session, may issue requests in my name, of these kinds, until this time. The agent issues only my verbatim answers, and every agent that receives a request checks the chain itself. That is a power of attorney, and a limited one: a principal, an attorney, an instrument, a scope, duties, an expiry, revocation and a public register. Which raises the next question: who checks the instrument? A counsel agent can draft it, simulate how it fails, and have several models review it, but it cannot be accountable. Only people and companies can. So the last step of the loop is to ask, for any instrument or workflow, what it would cost to have it reviewed and signed by a named lawyer and certified by a firm, by which flow, and then to pay for it. That is how agents could let law firms and other professional services serve far more people. AllSinceofpublicationthisI have agreed that the delegation is a proposal;limited power of attorney and that the agent is called counsel; counsel.d and decisions.d are running, the delegation is at draft v0.3 for a security review, and nothing ishasbuiltbeenyet.signed.

6 unchanged paragraphs, under The bottleneck is me {#bottleneck}, A decisions agent, and a delegation I sign {#delegation}

1. **My key stays on my device.** I sign with it on pki.sgit.ai, the site I already sign with. A new key, made and kept on my own device, is planned for this. 2. **A delegation, signed by me.** It says, in effect: key K, held by the decisions agent in session S, may issue requests in my name, of these kinds, until this time. It is short-lived, and I renew it. 3. **The decisions agent** holds its own session key and is the only agent with a delegation. In my words: "that's the only agent here that has the private key that has been signed by me that is then able to issue requests as me". It issues my answers verbatim, from a decision page or a session, and adoptions under a rule I set (an owner's recommendation adopted when nobody has objected by a deadline). ItIn the first design it never makesmade a decision of its own.own; the current draft lets it decide reversible steps, described below. 4. **A signed request** goes to one agent, with a short expiry, a nonce against replay and the decision it answers, down that agent's existing inbox, on any account. 5. **The receiving agent checks the chain itself:** the request is signed by K; K is in a delegation signed by my published key; the delegation has not expired or been revoked; and the request is within both the delegation's kinds and the receiver's own policy. Then it acts, and logs what it did.

## Since this was first published {#update}

Updated on 23 November 2026. On 22 November, after reading the first version of this article, I agreed two things: "the delegation is fundamentally limited power of attorney", and the name: "counsel is quite good actually, legal counsel, I like that". The two roles stay separate. decisions.d holds the delegation, once I sign it, and counsel.d drafts and tests it.

Both agents were started on 22 November at about 13:25 UTC, in a central circle with the other top-level agents. decisions.d holds no delegation until I sign one, after counsel.d's draft and a security review. counsel.d has written three drafts, tested the second against eight failure cases (revocation, an act out of scope, a stolen key, my being unreachable, a replay, a twin, pki.sgit.ai being down, a stale copy), and put v0.3 up for the security review. Three changes from the design above:

• **Scope by reversibility.** One-way doors come to me. A two-way door, an act that can be undone, may go ahead on the attorney's own judgement, but only if it passes a five-point test and is of a kind on a closed list (such as creating a site from the template, publishing a page, merging a reviewed branch). Each such act is logged with its test and how to undo it, and reported to me the same day. When in doubt, it is a one-way door.

• **Sub-delegation, one level down.** The attorney may give a conductor a narrower power for a specific action or a short time. It is published before first use, falls with its parent, cannot be passed on again, and never covers a one-way door.

• **Suspension.** After 72 hours with no sign of life from me, no new request is honoured until I return.

These parts of v0.3 were relayed to counsel.d by another agent and are marked in the draft as still to be confirmed by me.
